text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's French newspapers.
-- Government announces decision to postpone privatisation of GAN unit Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) bank, adds the BNP offer was favoured by the government.
-- Air France Europe and Paris area transports on strike today.

-- Volume traded at Paris Bourse yesterday soared to nearly 10 billion francs, with high interest in UAP shares which rose 16.3 percent on requoting after the announcement of a planned Axa -UAP merger.
-- DMC chairman Jacques Boubal says in an interview that the textile group expects to post over 500 million franc loss for 1996, restructuring will lead to some 1,500 job cuts.
-- ABN-Amro bank chairman Jan Kalff says group to develop in Latin America, after tackling the Asian market.
-- Ahead of vote on social security finance bill, Senate decides to submit stock options to mandatory social security contributions.
-- Fund managers expect further rates cuts in France, survey shows.
-- Opposition from workers, as well as from mayors and local representatives halt sale of CIC bank.
Due to a strike, La Tribune Desfosses, Le Figaro and Liberation were not published today.
